title: Program Manager, Strategy and Operations, Google Arts and Culture
descriptionHtml:
A problem isn’t truly solved until it’s solved for all. That’s why Googlers build products that help create opportunities for everyone, whether down the street or across the globe. As a Program Manager at Google, you’ll lead complex, multi-disciplinary projects from start to finish — working with stakeholders to plan requirements, manage project schedules, identify risks, and communicate clearly with cross-functional partners across the company. Your projects will often span offices, time zones, and hemispheres. It's your job to coordinate the players and keep them up to date on progress and deadlines.

As a Program Manager on the Google Arts and Culture (GAC) team, you will sit at the intersection of strategy and operations, acting as a critical bridge between GAC leadership, product teams, cross-functional partners, and global external cultural organizations. By driving rigorous metrics tracking and process improvements, you will ensure that our teams are aligned and operating efficiently. You will act as the connective tissue across the organization, translating high-level strategy into actionable operational plans and fostering a culture of operational excellence.

GAC is a cross-functional product group at Google. Our mission is to preserve, promote, and democratize access to culture. Together with museums, cultural institutions, and artists we bring the world's cultural heritage online and make immersive experiences available to anyone, anywhere.

Responsibilities

  • Drive the strategic planning rhythms for GAC, including the development, reviewing, and tracking of goals across the organization. Oversee budget planning, allocation, and tracking, ensuring resources are optimally deployed in alignment with top-line strategic goals.
  • Partner closely with cross-functional teams (including Product, Engineering, Content, Marketing) to align strategic priorities, unblock execution, and ensure seamless collaboration.
  • Act as a reliable operational contact for external strategic partners (museums, artists, scientific institutions), ensuring operational milestones and contract requirements are met.
  • Prepare clear, concise, and structured weekly status reports, budget updates, and executive briefs for executive leadership and key stakeholders.
  • Manage partnerships, program lifecycles, establish and track program metrics, and identify opportunities to improve tools and processes for team efficiency. Monitor, evaluate, and communicate program progress; apply best practices and internal tools to drive experiment velocity and operational efficiency.

Minimum qualifications:

  • Bachelor's degree in Business, Technology, Operations, or equivalent practical experience.
  • 2 years of experience in program management, business operations, or strategy and operations, with ownership of end-to-end program lifecycles.
  • Experience managing program budgets, financial tracking, and resource allocation (e.g., forecasting, tracking burn rates, agreement milestones).
  • Experience defining, tracking, and reporting operational and performance metrics (e.g., Objectives and Key Results (OKRs) and Key Performance Indicators (KPIs)) for executive leadership.
  • Experience driving cross-functional alignment across technical (engineering/product) and non-technical stakeholders (e.g., partnerships, content, or external institutions).

Preferred qualifications:

  • Experience in Business Operations and Strategy (BizOps), central PMO, or strategy and operations within a fast-paced technology company, leading cultural institution, or management consultancy.
  • Experience managing complex agreements and strategic external partnerships with global cultural or public institutions (museums, research centers, foundations, academic bodies).
  • Strong analytical and financial modeling skills, with proficiency in advanced sheets/spreadsheet software, SQL, or dashboarding tools.
  • Experience working with emerging technologies, specifically managing projects or operations that intersect with AI/ML, creative tech, or digital innovation.
  • Exceptional communication skills, with experience synthesizing complex technical, financial, and strategic data into crisp C-level memos, and weekly operational updates.

title: Account Strategist, Engage Sales, Google Customer Solutions
descriptionHtml:
Businesses of all shapes and sizes rely on Google’s unparalleled advertising solutions to help them grow in today's dynamic marketing environment. You bring a passion for sales, knowledge of online media, and commitment to maximize customer success. You act like an owner, move with velocity through change, finding innovative and strategic ways to consistently deliver extraordinary and incremental outcomes for both Google and your customers. You build trusted relationships with customers, uncovering their business needs and translating them into powerful solutions to achieve their most ambitious goals. You achieve as a team with sellers, shape the future of advertising in the AI-era, and make a real impact on the millions of companies and billions of users that trust Google with their most important goals.

Google Customer Solutions (GCS) sales teams are trusted advisors and competitive sellers who maintain a relentless focus on customer success by bringing the best Google has to offer to small- and medium-sized businesses (SMBs), which are the backbone of our communities. As a member of our team, you’ll have the opportunity to work with company owners and make a real difference in their businesses by helping them grow. Together, we help shape the future of innovation for customers, partners, and sellers...and we have fun doing it.Individual pay is determined by factors including job-related skills, experience, and relevant education or training.

Canada: $114000 - $116000 (CAD) + 35% bonus target + equity + benefits

Learn more about benefits at Google.

Responsibilities

  • Engage and influence key customer stakeholders by leading tactical meetings to uncover marketing goals and key performance indicators, translating them into actionable campaign strategies.
  • Drive exceptional campaign results, quantify business impact, and demonstrate value to customers, maintaining account hygiene.
  • Build and pitch data-driven solutions to maximize customer value through Google’s advertising solutions, handle objections, and ultimately achieve business growth goals.
  • Analyze campaign data, ensuring performance is accurately tracked, and delivering measurable results aligned with customer objectives.
  • Monitor performance data to extract key insights, identifying and cultivating qualified opportunities to drive future customer growth and build pipelines.

Minimum qualifications:

  • Bachelor's degree or equivalent practical experience.
  • 2 years of experience in advertising, consultative sales, business development, online media environment, or a marketing role.

Preferred qualifications:

  • Master's degree in a Business related field.
  • 2 years of experience working in a cross-functional organization.
  • 1 year of experience managing digital marketing and advertising campaigns, projects, and relationships with customers or agencies.
  • Experience building solutions using AI technologies.

title: Market Consultant, AUNZ (Fixed-Term Contract)
descriptionHtml:
People Operations strives to revolutionize human resources the same way that Google has revolutionized search. We are helping to find, grow and keep the remarkable assemblage of talent who are our Googlers. You'll be an advocate of Google's culture and values, partnering with our business leaders to help them build their organizations and make sure all people decisions are based on data. Whether coaching our clients on how to lead their teams, navigating and resolving employee relations issues or managing programs that help develop our Googlers, you are exceptionally focused on putting them first, and being as clear and transparent as possible to help Googlers understand how people decisions get made.

Our Market Consultant role is known for deep subject matter expertise in HR programs, processes, and execution in their particular market. They work closely with the Head of HR, who sets the strategy via the Market HR Plan, to execute on and operationalize Google’s geographic priorities. Market consultants have sound knowledge of company and local programs, policies, and compliance procedures, and offer a compelling voice around HR matters internally and externally. They use their influencing skills to represent the needs of Google, facilitate partner discussions, and drive decisions that bring stakeholders along using change management skills.

Responsibilities

  • Work with the relevant teams to ensure end-to-end delivery for our HR processes in country, in particular with a focus on minimizing HR compliance risks and managing labor relations risks and related work.
  • Contribute to the deployment of high-priority country-focused HR programs and initiatives aligned to the country People plan (e.g., flexible work, psychosocial frameworks, new entity setup, onboarding, RTW providers).
  • Manage local employment policies and practices to ensure legal and regulatory compliance (e.g., LSL).
  • Work with the HR compliance team, process ownership team, user support team, and the relevant COE teams on prioritizing and mitigating market-related risks.
  • Drive recommendations and prioritization to ensure work is in service of the end-to-end delivery of our Googler experience in the country.

Minimum qualifications:

  • Bachelor's degree in Human Resources, Labor Relations, or equivalent practical experience.
  • 7 years of HR Business Partner or HR Generalist experience.


Preferred qualifications:

  • Experience implementing HR projects including risk management/mitigation, new entity set up, change management, business readiness, communications, and training activities.
  • Experience Managing HR risks and compliance including identifying risks and need and developing a mitigation plan.
  • Experience leading businesses and HR strategies across both Australia and New Zealand.
  • Demonstrated experience with cross-functional collaboration and drive decisions with multiple stakeholder groups.
  • Broad range of HR knowledge, with experience with consultation processes and Labour Relations exposure to CoE disciplines and local employment law.
  • Strong project management skills and delivery, able to manage multiple simultaneous priorities.

title: Partner Solutions Architect, Ecosystem Engineer Data Systems
descriptionHtml:
It's an exciting time to join Google Cloud’s Go-To-Market team, leading the AI revolution for businesses worldwide. You’ll leverage Google's brand credibility—a legacy built on inventing foundational technologies and proven at scale. We’ll provide you with the world's most advanced AI portfolio, including frontier Gemini models, and the complete Vertex AI platform, helping you to solve business problems. We’re a collaborative culture providing direct access to DeepMind's engineering and research minds, empowering you to solve customer challenges. Join us to be the catalyst for our mission, drive customer success, and define the new cloud era—the market is yours. Individual pay is determined by factors including job-related skills, experience, and relevant education or training.

US: $183000 - $265000 (USD) + 20% bonus target + equity + benefits

Learn more about benefits at Google.

Responsibilities

  • Build reusable data-to-AI solutions, architectures, and accelerators with partners on Google Cloud.
  • Design and implement governed semantic layers and enterprise ontologies connecting BigQuery Graph, Conversational Analytics Agents, Looker, and Google Cloud Knowledge Catalog Custom Aspects to ground enterprise AI agents in verified business definitions.
  • Validate Gemini Enterprise plugins, remote Model Context Protocol. (MCP) servers, and reusable agent skills that integrate Google Data Cloud services with third-party enterprise systems.
  • Develop internal AI-assisted validation tools, evaluation rubrics, and automated architectural review workflows that scale Partner Engineering quality and turnaround velocity across partner engagements.
  • Lead technical onboarding for Data and AI launches, developing implementation guides, code assets, and enablement materials.

Minimum qualifications:

  • Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Data Science, Engineering, or a related technical field, or equivalent practical experience.
  • 7 years of experience in customer or partner-facing technical roles such as Solutions Architect, Partner Engineer, Customer Engineer, or Principal Data Architect in a cloud computing environment.
  • Experience with enterprise data platforms, analytical data warehousing, relational and non-relational databases, and real-time data pipelines (e.g., BigQuery, Spanner, AlloyDB, Pub/Sub, Dataflow, Spark, or equivalent cloud data services).
  • Experience building solutions with Large Language Models (LLMs), agentic frameworks (e.g., Google ADK, LangGraph), or Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) architectures using Python, SQL, Go, or Java.

Preferred qualifications:

  • Experience developing Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers, Agent-to-Agent (A2A) integrations, or enterprise agent plugins for Global System Integrators (GSIs) or SaaS Independent Software Vendor (ISVs).
  • Experience leading cross-organizational technical programs with GSIs and translating repeatable field patterns into reusable partner code repositories and technical guides.
  • Experience defining technical strategy and influencing executive leaders within global partner organizations.
  • Expertise in Google Cloud's data analytics, database, and AI/ML platforms and services.
  • Proven track record of migrating and modernizing complex on-premises or multi-cloud data estates (e.g., Snowflake, Databricks, Teradata, Oracle) on Google Cloud and activating them for AI workloads.

title: Data Cloud Sales Specialist III, Google Cloud (Spanish, English)
descriptionHtml:
As a Data Cloud Sales Specialist, you will be at the forefront of driving Google Cloud's most critical data and AI growth. In this role, you will drive growth by securing new greenfield logos and identify untapped, uncommitted workloads. You will partner with Field Sales Representatives, Customer Engineers, and Partners to execute joint Data+AI plays that establish long-term data platform standardization.

You will be a master of value-selling. You will engage with line-of-business (LoB) leaders, CDO, CAIO, and CFO to discover critical pain points, build robust business cases (ROI/TCO reduction), and demonstrate the quantifiable business value of modernizing data estates on GCP.

Additionally, you will guide technical stakeholders and position Google Cloud's Agentic Data Cloud suite (BigQuery, Knowledge Catalog, Borderless Lakehouse, Spanner, AlloyDB) as the premium data intelligence platform for AI. You will present demos that showcase how unified, well-governed data foundations power secure, hallucination-free AI agents and real-time experiences.Google Cloud accelerates every organization’s ability to digitally transform its business and industry. We deliver enterprise-grade solutions that leverage Google’s cutting-edge technology, and tools that help developers build more sustainably. Customers in more than 200 countries and territories turn to Google Cloud as their trusted partner to enable growth and solve their most critical business problems.

Responsibilities

  • Deliver against quota and achieve or exceed strategic business and growth goals. Drive new greenfield logos and workloads in existing accounts through proactive campaigns.
  • Run complex, multi-threaded business cycles from initial discovery and value hypothesis to ROI business case creation and commercial close.
  • Engage Line of Business leaders, Chief Data Officer, Chief Financial Officer, Chief Marketing Officer, Chief AI Officer, through value-selling, tying modern Data and AI capabilities to quantified business outcomes.
  • Align cross-functionally with FSRs and Partners to execute joint Data+AI plays, driving platform standardization and co-sell motions.
  • Whiteboard modern architectures (BigQuery, Spark, Spanner, AlloyDB) to demonstrate how unified data foundations power high-performance, hallucination-free AI agents.

Minimum qualifications:

  • Bachelor's degree or equivalent practical experience.
  • 10 years of quota-carrying enterprise sales experience.
  • Experience building business cases through workshops or product demos to business executives.
  • Experience developing partnerships with technical stakeholders (e.g., Enterprise Architects, Data Engineers, Data Scientists).
  • Experience positioning and selling technical solutions in data management, analytics, infrastructure, or AI/ML.
  • Ability to communicate in Spanish and English fluently to support client relationship management in this region.

Preferred qualifications:

  • Experience positioning modern cloud data platforms, lakehouses, real-time streaming, or GenAI platforms against legacy or other proprietary enterprise systems.
  • Experience working with Global System Integrators, hyperscalers, or ISVs to co-sell and accelerate pipeline.
  • Experience closing large-scale data and AI transformation deals within specific regulated or high-growth enterprise verticals (e.g., Financial Services, Healthcare/Life Sciences, Retail, or Manufacturing).
  • Understanding of how modern cloud architectures, data governance (e.g., cataloging, lineage, compliance), and clean data estates enable AI and real-time analytics.

title: Associate Product Manager, University Graduate, 2027 Start
descriptionHtml:
At Google, we put our users first. The world is always changing, so we need Product Managers who are continuously adapting and excited to work on products that affect millions of people every day.

In this role, you will work cross-functionally to guide products from conception to launch by connecting the technical and business worlds. You can break down complex problems into steps that drive product development.

One of the many reasons Google consistently brings innovative, world-changing products to market is because of the collaborative work we do in Product Management. Our team works closely with creative engineers, designers, marketers, etc. to help design and develop technologies that improve access to the world's information. We're responsible for guiding products throughout the execution cycle, focusing specifically on analyzing, positioning, packaging, promoting, and tailoring our solutions to our users.

Google aims to build products that organize the world's information and make it universally accessible to our users. As a Product Manager at Google, you could be working on new technologies, platforms, consumer facing products, and/or enterprise systems. The end goal will be to match you with the team that best aligns with your interests, experience, and where you will have the most impact.

Responsibilities

  • Understand markets and user requirements in depth.
  • Launch products and features, test their performance, and iterate quickly.
  • Work collaboratively with Engineering, Marketing, Legal, and User Experience (UX) on technologies.
  • Develop innovative solutions to problems by collaborating as needed across regions, product areas, and functions.

Minimum qualifications:

  • Currently enrolled in or graduated from a degree program within Product Management, Computer Science, Engineering, Data Science, Mathematics, Statistics, or a related technical field, or equivalent practical experience.
  • Internship or Teaching Assistant experience in product management, software development or a similar technical field.
  • Experience leading entrepreneurial efforts or outreach within organizations while building cross-functional relationships.
  • Experience preparing and delivering technical presentations to an audience through internships, coursework, or extracurriculars.

Preferred qualifications:

  • Experience with methodologies aimed to drive product development and delivery.
  • Experience applying Artificial Intelligence/Machine Learning (AI/ML) concepts to build products or features through relevant internship, capstone projects, or other academic work.
  • Technical experience with programming languages, data analysis, business case/modeling, pricing, or design.
  • Ability to start full-time in the primary cohort onboarding cycle between April and August 2027.
  • Ability to communicate in English fluently to support cross-functional business relationships in the region.
  • Excellent problem-solving, organizational, investigative, and critical thinking skills.

title: Strategic Partner Development Manager, Google Payment (Japanese, English)
descriptionHtml:
Google's line of products and services to our clients never stops growing. The Partnerships Development team is responsible for seeking and exploring new opportunities with Google's partners. Equipped with your business acumen and extensive product knowledge, you are right on the front line of interacting with our partners, and helping them find ways to grow using Google's newest product offerings. Your knowledge of relevant verticals and relationships with key industry players will help shape our great applications and content for products such as YouTube, Google TV and Commerce. Google’s Global Partnerships team powers extraordinary user experiences through partnerships that solve users’ needs, advance our partners’ goals, and further Google’s mission. Our team provides meaningful solutions — from helping publishers and developers grow their businesses through monetization solutions, to helping our long-term partners anticipate and navigate change in a way that delivers economic and reputational value. We build and distribute products through partnerships across a multitude of product areas, including Ads, Search & Assistant, Geo, Platforms & Ecosystems, Devices & Services, Health, Retail, Payments, Next Billion Users, and more. We collaborate across Google, ensuring a coordinated approach when engaging with our most complex and strategic partners.

Responsibilities

  • Manage relationships with multiple high-stakes partners and drive partner engagement and development across the Japanese payment ecosystem (e.g., payment networks, banks, issuers, acquirers, processors, merchants).
  • Guide the integration of multiple adjacent partner plan timelines, goals, and objectives, and manage account priorities and resource allocation in line with long-term strategy.
  • Contribute to the identification, creation, negotiation, and implementation of effective business development agreements that drive results for Google (e.g., bilateral agreements, standardized partner agreements).
  • Drive cross-functional/cross-regional engagement with teams including Strategy, Finance, Legal, Product, Engineering, Marketing, Operations, Android, Cloud, and Ads to deliver on key product objectives and One Google wins.
  • Identify opportunities to grow business within the ecosystem, help resolve complex partner issues (e.g., business and technical), and build repeatable processes for future scalability.

Minimum qualifications:

  • Bachelor's degree or equivalent practical experience.
  • 7 years of experience in business development, partnerships, management consulting, or investment banking.
  • Experience working with C-level executives and cross-functionally across all levels of management.
  • Experience managing agreements or partnerships.
  • Ability to communicate in Japanese and English fluently to interact with internal and external stakeholders.

Preferred qualifications:

  • Experience working in or with the financial services sector or the e-commerce ecosystem in Japan.
  • Experience driving results across technical and business domains in a matrixed organization.
  • Previous experience negotiating partnership agreements with financial institutions or merchants.
  • In-depth knowledge of digital payments, loyalty ecosystems, and the financial industry.
  • Ability to work autonomously and collaboratively within ambiguous, constantly evolving environments.
  • Demonstrated partnership, relationship-building, and project management skills with internal stakeholders and external partners, with the ability to influence without authority.

title: Engineering Manager, Cloud Support Platform
descriptionHtml:
Google Cloud’s mission is to make every business successful through AI by combining cutting-edge technology, infrastructure, and talent. AI/ML software engineers in Cloud bridge the gap between pioneering models and a massive product vehicle reaching billions. Our talent density and AI-powered tools drive rapid development, rooted in a culture of empowerment and a bias to action. In this role, you aren’t just building technology; you’re shaping the frontier of enterprise and driving the evolution of advanced models.

This is a unique opportunity to have a large impact driving Cloud’s growth and impact the customer and internal agent experience through multiple initiatives. Initiatives not only allows you to help shape the outlook and roadmap of the Cloud Support Platform and its implementation in phases, but also allows you to collaborate with many Cloud Product and Business teams and provide a unique opportunity to learn about multiple products and business processes across major Cloud product areas.

As Engineering Manager, you will be passionate about helping customer be successful in their Cloud journey and accelerate Google Cloud's growth through building solutions/systems. Cloud Support Platform (CSP) is working initiatives to contribute to the growth for Google Cloud. These initiatives range helping customers get better support to driving Cloud's adoption. This role will require involvement in shaping product outlook and delivering these initiatives by partnering with product and other engineering teams.

Individual pay is determined by factors including job-related skills, experience, and relevant education or training.

US: $207000 - $300000 (USD) + 20% bonus target + equity + benefits

Learn more about benefits at Google.

Responsibilities

  • Lead the CSP technical outlook, roadmap, and resilient architecture, directly influencing the broader Google Cloud strategy.
  • Partner with business stakeholders to balance technology investments across agent workflows, automation, and incident management.
  • Direct end-to-end software development, driving robust design, operations, and impactful, high-quality product launches.
  • Build and mentor a high-performing engineering organization through effective coaching, strategies, and succession planning.
  • Partner with product manager, program management, and peer teams to resolve complex issues efficiently and deliver an innovative customer experience.

Minimum qualifications:

  • Bachelor’s degree or equivalent practical experience.
  • 8 years of experience in software development.
  • Experience in technical leadership, leading project teams, and setting technical direction.
  • Experience in people management.

Preferred qualifications:

  • Master's degree or PhD in related field.
  • 3 years of experience in direct technical leadership and people management.
  • Experience in software development using one or more general-purpose programming languages (e.g., C/C++, Java, Go).

title: Technical Program Manager, Global Network Acquisition, Metro Planner
descriptionHtml:
A problem isn’t truly solved until it’s solved for all. That’s why Googlers build products that help create opportunities for everyone, whether down the street or across the globe. As a Technical Program Manager at Google, you’ll use your technical expertise to lead complex, multi-disciplinary projects from start to finish. You’ll work with stakeholders to plan requirements, identify risks, manage project schedules, and communicate clearly with cross-functional partners across the company. You're equally comfortable explaining your team's analyses and recommendations to executives as you are discussing the technical tradeoffs in product development with engineers.

In this technical program management role, you will own and drive the strategic network planning direction for the region projects for the EMEA Network Acquisitions (GNA).

This position is highly analytical, involving data-driven analysis to develop the metro’s roadmap, compiling the strategic vision in supporting the network assets procurement plan such as RSP, fiber and leased wavelengths in order to meet forecast demand and the business strategy, while complying and influencing network architecture guidelines. You will be expected to optimize Google’s Production Network for scalability, reliability, and cost efficiency while maintaining the ability to meet new product rollout in a timely manner. This will be accomplished by enabling close cross-functional collaboration and teamwork with network engineers, strategic negotiators, and varying TPgMs across multiple teams.

The AI and Infrastructure team is redefining what’s possible. We empower Google customers with breakthrough capabilities and insights by delivering AI and Infrastructure at unparalleled scale, efficiency, reliability and velocity. Our customers include Googlers, Google Cloud customers, and billions of Google users worldwide.

We're the driving force behind Google's groundbreaking innovations, empowering the development of our cutting-edge AI models, delivering unparalleled computing power to global services, and providing the essential platforms that enable developers to build the future. From software to hardware our teams are shaping the future of world-leading hyperscale computing, with key teams working on the development of our TPUs, Vertex AI for Google Cloud, Google Global Networking, Data Center operations, systems research, and much more.

Individual pay is determined by factors including job-related skills, experience, and relevant education or training.

Ireland: €118000 - €120000 (EUR) + 15% bonus target + equity + benefits

Learn more about benefits at Google.

Responsibilities

  • Architect three-year infrastructure roadmaps alongside cross-functional partners to scale regional capacity, control costs, and support asset procurement for deal approvals.
  • Deliver deep technical risk assessments through extensive "what-if" analyses, ensuring resilient, high-performance network design choices across the entire footprint.
  • Interface with internal business owners to capture capacity drivers and deadlines, coordinating closely with deployment and engineering teams to track end-to-end progress.
  • Partner across technical teams to refine planning workflows, reduce delivery lead times, and integrate AI into tooling to enhance data integrity.
  • Ingest and translate regional demand flows into optimized Layer 0 and Layer 3 asset plans, factoring in market trends and technology evolution.

Minimum qualifications:

  • Bachelor's degree in a technical field, or equivalent practical experience.
  • 5 years of experience in program management.
  • Experience in network infrastructure, network design, network architecture, optical design, and fiber architecture.

Preferred qualifications:

  • Experience in IP, OSP, optical networking design and planning.
  • Experience with program management in the networking area and in delivering infrastructure assets and vendor management.
  • Ability to learn and balance business and technical understanding to drive the long-term objectives of the organization.
  • Strong problem solving skills, with ability to adopt a data-driven, analytical approach towards solving complex challenges.
  • Strong communication skills and collaboration with a diverse range of people and job functions.

title: Software Engineer, Generative Media AI, Apparel ML
descriptionHtml:
Google's software engineers develop the next-generation technologies that change how billions of users connect, explore, and interact with information and one another. Our products need to handle information at massive scale, and extend well beyond web search. We're looking for engineers who bring fresh ideas from all areas, including information retrieval, distributed computing, large-scale system design, networking and data storage, security, artificial intelligence, natural language processing, UI design and mobile; the list goes on and is growing every day. As a software engineer, you will work on a specific project critical to Google’s needs with opportunities to switch teams and projects as you and our fast-paced business grow and evolve. We need our engineers to be versatile, display leadership qualities and be enthusiastic to take on new problems across the full-stack as we continue to push technology forward.

As a part of this team, you will focus on productionizing GenAI shopping features across Google’s most prominent surfaces, including Search, Commerce, Ads, Chrome, and YouTube. Here, you will master the art of scaling multimodal GenAI to production-level quality, leveraging Google’s infrastructure to deliver highly customized, industry-defining user experiences.

Google Ads is at the forefront of AI innovation, applying cutting-edge machine learning and Generative AI models like Gemini to power a multi-billion dollar global business.

Our work directly impacts billions of users by protecting users from harm, improving ad quality, and optimizing campaigns for advertiser return-on-investment. We foster a culture of deep collaboration, partnering closely with teams like Google Research and DeepMind to solve complex challenges. Join us to work on state-of-the-art AI, take on problems at an unparalleled scale, and build the next generation of advertising technology.

Individual pay is determined by factors including job-related skills, experience, and relevant education or training.

US: $147000 - $210000 (USD) + 15% bonus target + equity + benefits

Learn more about benefits at Google.

Responsibilities

  • Write product or system development code.
  • Collaborate with peers and stakeholders through design and code reviews to ensure best practices amongst available technologies (e.g., style guidelines, checking code in, accuracy, testability, and efficiency).
  • Contribute to existing documentation or educational content and adapt content based on product/program updates and user feedback.
  • Triage product or system issues and debug/track/resolve by analyzing the sources of issues and the impact on hardware, network, or service operations and quality.
  • Implement solutions in one or more specialized ML areas, utilize ML infrastructure, and contribute to model optimization and data processing.

Minimum qualifications:

  • Bachelor’s degree or equivalent practical experience.
  • 2 years of experience with software development in one or more programming languages, or 1 year of experience with an advanced degree.
  • 1 year of experience with ML infrastructure (e.g., model deployment, model evaluation, optimization, data processing, debugging).

Preferred qualifications:

  • Master's degree or PhD in Computer Science or related technical fields.
  • 2 years of experience with data structures and algorithms.
  • Experience with image processing, computer vision, or machine learning applications.

title: Outcome Customer Engineer, Google Cloud Platform Delivery (Turkish, English)
descriptionHtml:
The Google Cloud Platform team helps customers transform and build what's next for their business — all with technology built in the cloud. Our products are developed for security, reliability and scalability, running the full stack from infrastructure to applications to devices and hardware. Our teams are dedicated to helping our customers — developers, small and large businesses, educational institutions and government agencies — see the benefits of our technology come to life. As part of an entrepreneurial team in this rapidly growing business, you will play a key role in understanding the needs of our customers and help shape the future of businesses of all sizes use technology to connect with customers, employees and partners.

As a Google Cloud Platform (GCP) Outcome Customer Engineer (OCE), you will drive initial and ongoing revenue ramp for our customers, clearing blockers and ensuring they get the maximum benefit from their investment faster. You will manage and execute the deployment plan, transitioning scoped workloads into production by providing technical leadership to customers and partners. You will have a direct impact on the velocity and incremental consumption of customer workloads, leading to accelerated value realization, higher adoption, and future expansion opportunities.

You will blend sales expertise, market knowledge, direct technical engagement, and technical project management to prove the value of the Google Cloud portfolio.

Google Cloud accelerates every organization’s ability to digitally transform its business and industry. We deliver enterprise-grade solutions that leverage Google’s cutting-edge technology, and tools that help developers build more sustainably. Customers in more than 200 countries and territories turn to Google Cloud as their trusted partner to enable growth and solve their most critical business problems.

Responsibilities

  • Develop and orchestrate a structured, end-to-end deployment plan across customer, professional services, and partner teams, onboarding the implementation team, clearing blockers, managing timelines and progress, and ensuring readiness (e.g., capacity, training).
  • Employ coding, debugging, or systems design to resolve technical blockers and accelerate deployment.
  • Drive and track progress of the initial and ongoing ramp of workloads, moving customers from agreement to consumption as quickly as possible.
  • Identify expansion opportunities for new workloads within the account during project execution.
  • Drive sustainable product usage to help customers realize value on an ongoing basis and secure future contract renewals.

Minimum qualifications:

  • Bachelor's degree or equivalent practical experience.
  • 6 years of experience with cloud native architecture in a customer-facing or support role.
  • Experience in deployment planning, orchestration, or change management.
  • Experience in programming languages, debugging, or systems design.
  • Experience engaging with, presenting to, or influencing technical stakeholders or executive leaders.
  • Ability to communicate in Turkish and English fluently to support the client relationship management in the region.

Preferred qualifications:

  • Experience selling technical solutions in one or more of the following areas: infrastructure modernization, application modernization, data management, data analytics, AI, networking, migrations or security.
  • Experience with Google Cloud products and differentiation from competition.
  • Experience working with product and capacity teams to resolve technical and capacity blockers.
  • Experience with object-oriented programming languages (i.e. Python, Java), and using technical proficiencies to remove blockers and accelerate customer deployment.

title: Open Source Intelligence Specialist, Sentinel, Collection Management
descriptionHtml:
As an Open Source Intelligence Specialist within the Sentinel Team, you will play a critical role in Google’s Global Security and Resilience Services (GSRS). Your primary mission is to identify, research, and assess potential threats to Google’s people, property, and interests by leveraging open-source data.

You will be responsible for the end-to-end intelligence cycle, from collection to dissemination, ensuring that leadership receives timely and accurate insights to inform incident response, crisis management, and global travel security. In this role, you will require a blend of technical Open Source Intelligence (OSINT) expertise, and the ability to operate in a dynamic environment.

From keeping Googlers safe and secure to managing disruptive events, the ability to anticipate, deter, detect, and act are the pillars of Google’s Global Security and Resilience Services (GSRS) team. title: Director, Technical Program Management, Manufacturing and Industrial Engineering
descriptionHtml:
The Modular Manufacturing & Integration organization is leading an industry-defining transformation in how Google delivers technical infrastructure for the AI era. Transitioning away from conventional, on-site, purpose-built construction, our mission is to industrialize data center delivery through mass-assembled, standardized modules and off-site manufacturing.

By pushing labor-intensive assembly, systems integration, and quality testing upstream into controlled factory environments, we enable "square wave" capacity delivery—turning on gigawatt-scale AI compute, liquid cooling, power distribution, and network fabric with unprecedented velocity. Operating across AI Systems & Infrastructure (AI2), Google Data Centers (GDC), Systems & Manufacturing (ISM), and Google Global Infrastructure (GGI), our team defines the modular technical product and serves as the accountable business owner for industrializing and landing modular capacity globally.

As the Principal TPM of Manufacturing & Industrial Engineering, you will be the chief industrial architect responsible for translating Google’s modular infrastructure strategy into an executable, manufacturing reality. In this principal technical leadership role—with the charter to incubate the discipline and potentially scale a dedicated team over time—you will bridge the gap between design engineering, external contract manufacturing, and on-site field execution.

Your remit spans the entire physical and technical stack: structural modules, medium-to-low voltage power skids, liquid cooling distribution, and dense AI compute hardware. You will evaluate current field deployment and operations bottlenecks and establish scalable manufacturing processes with global contract manufacturers and fabricators. Your core mandate is simple yet radical: dramatically compress the timeline from factory gate to live AI compute, reduce complexity of assembly in manufacturing and in the field, and increase first pass yield/quality of the entire data center system.

The AI and Infrastructure team is redefining what’s possible. We empower Google customers with breakthrough capabilities and insights by delivering AI and Infrastructure at unparalleled scale, efficiency, reliability and velocity. Our customers include Googlers, Google Cloud customers, and billions of Google users worldwide.

We're the driving force behind Google's groundbreaking innovations, empowering the development of our cutting-edge AI models, delivering unparalleled computing power to global services, and providing the essential platforms that enable developers to build the future. From software to hardware our teams are shaping the future of world-leading hyperscale computing, with key teams working on the development of our TPUs, Vertex AI for Google Cloud, Google Global Networking, Data Center operations, systems research, and much more.

Individual pay is determined by factors including job-related skills, experience, and relevant education or training.

US: $281000 - $391000 (USD) + 30% bonus target + equity + benefits

Learn more about benefits at Google.

Responsibilities

  • Formulate and drive the multi-year manufacturing and assembly roadmap for Google’s modular data center platforms, aligning complex system architectures with industrial factory capabilities.
  • Deconstruct monolithic data center systems into standardized, manufactured building blocks. Architect module boundaries across structural, cooling, power, and IT server clusters to maximize factory pre-assembly and minimize field connections.
  • Advocate for DFM/A, Design for Test (DFT), and modular interface standards upstream across Hardware Engineering, Data Center Engineering, and Infrastructure design teams, ensuring products are engineered from inception for rapid off-site assembly.
  • Dive into existing on-site data center construction, white-space fit-out, and compute commissioning processes. Identify labor-intensive operations and re-engineer them into off-site, factory-integrated steps.

Minimum qualifications:

  • Bachelor's degree in Industrial Engineering, Manufacturing Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Systems Engineering, or equivalent practical experience.
  • 15 years of technical program management, manufacturing engineering, or industrial engineering experience spanning integrated physical/hardware systems.
  • 10 years of experience applying Design for Manufacturing and Assembly (DFM/A), Lean Manufacturing, and process optimization to electromechanical or mission-critical systems.
  • 10 years of experience working directly with external Contract Manufacturers (CMs), Original Design Manufacturers (ODMs), or specialized industrial fabricators to stand up assembly and test lines.

Preferred qualifications:

  • Master’s degree or PhD in Industrial Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Operations Research, or an MBA with a technical undergraduate degree.
  • 15 years of experience leading industrialization and manufacturing programs for low-to-mid volume, highly complex capital systems (e.g., aerospace systems integration, semiconductor capital equipment, specialized defense systems, complex power/propulsion plants, or modular high-performance compute clusters).
  • Deep technical literacy across both facility infrastructure (structural enclosures, liquid cooling loops, high-power distribution skids) and IT compute hardware (TPU/GPU server trays, rack-level integration, cabling topologies, and L11/L12 assembly).

descriptionHtml:

Beam is an AI-first 3D video communication platform developed by Google that enables remote conversations to feel like natural, in-person interactions. Formerly known as Project Starline, Beam combines advanced AI volumetric video modeling, spatial audio, and light-field display technology to provide lifelike depth, perspective, and eye contact without requiring headsets or 3D glasses. title: Data Center Facilities Technician, Mechanical

title: Security Engineer, Third Party Security Diligence
descriptionHtml:
There's no such thing as a "safe system" - only safer systems. Our Security team works to create and maintain the safest operating environment for Google's users and developers. As a Security Engineer, you help protect network boundaries, keep computer systems and network devices hardened against attacks and provide security services to protect highly sensitive data like passwords and customer information. Security Engineers work directly with network equipment and actively monitor our systems for attacks and intrusions. You also work with software engineers to proactively identify and fix security flaws and vulnerabilities.

You use your industry experience to own and drive the resolution of complex security incidents, policy questions and technical security issues.

SPMA (Security and Privacy for Mergers, Acquisitions and Alphabet) team’s mandate is focused on reducing Acquisitions, third-party and Cloud risk to Google and Alphabet.

SPMA executes on its mandate through three key verticals:

  • Mergers, Acquisitions and Alphabets (M&A): Effectively and safely raise the security bar for Google’s Off Google entities (Acquisitions and Bets); helping companies navigate Google’s security landscape and processes, thereby safely and securely integrating/divesting/separating them.
  • Alphabet Use of Cloud (AUC): Manage and minimize risk from Alphabet’s use of public clouds (GCP).
  • Third-party/Vendor Security Diligence (3PSD): Ensure effective governance and minimize risk from Alphabet’s use of third-party vendors.
This role sits within the Third Party/Vendor Security Diligence (3PSD) vertical, focusing on third-party security. Alphabet’s Third Party Security Diligence program ensures security of our third-party engagements, and is part of a broader third-party risk management ecosystem.

The Core team builds the technical foundation behind Google’s flagship products. We are owners and advocates for the underlying design elements, developer platforms, product components, and infrastructure at Google. These are the essential building blocks for excellent, safe, and coherent experiences for our users and drive the pace of innovation for every developer. We look across Google’s products to build central solutions, break down technical barriers and strengthen existing systems. As the Core team, we have a mandate and a unique opportunity to impact important technical decisions across the company.

Responsibilities

  • Conduct comprehensive security diligence for critical and high-risk third-party vendors, evaluating their controls against Google's requirements, identifying risks, and recommending remediation.
  • Contribute to the engineering improvement of the Third Party Security Diligence (3PSD) program by developing tools, automation, and proposing process enhancements.
  • Assist in technically integrating 3PSD tools with the wider OneTPRM ecosystem and support data analysis to identify risk trends.
  • Collaborate with and provide security guidance to internal stakeholders like vendor managers and Product teams on third-party engagements.
  • Develop and maintain deep technical expertise in security domains relevant to third-party risk (e.g., cloud, application security, IAM) and help create reusable security patterns and best practices.

Minimum qualifications:

  • Bachelor's degree or equivalent practical experience.
  • 2 years of experience with security assessments or security design reviews or threat modeling.
  • 2 years of experience with security engineering, computer and network security and security protocols.
  • 2 years of experience coding in one or more general purpose languages (e.g., Python, SQL, C, C++, Java, Go).

Preferred qualifications:

  • Demonstrated experience and strong background in relevant enterprise security domains, particularly in threat modeling, security assessments, authentication and access controls, SaaS security, cloud security and data protection.
  • Experience with security engineering, security architecture or consulting.
  • Proven ability to independently produce high-quality engineering artifacts (e.g., design docs, code reviews, or risk assessments) that require minimal revision.
  • Ability to drive and deliver risk reduction outcomes with high autonomy and limited oversight.
  • Excellent verbal and written communication skills.

title: Senior Software Engineer, Pixel Security and Privacy
locations: New Taipei, Banqiao District, New Taipei City, Taiwan
descriptionHtml:

Our products need to handle information at massive scale, and extend well beyond web search. We're looking for engineers who bring fresh ideas from all areas, including information retrieval, distributed computing, large-scale system design, networking and data storage, security, artificial intelligence, natural language processing, UI design and mobile; the list goes on and is growing every day. As a software engineer, you will work on a specific project critical to Google’s needs with opportunities to switch teams and projects as you and our fast-paced business grow and evolve. We need our engineers to be versatile, display leadership qualities and be enthusiastic to take on new problems across the full-stack as we continue to push technology forward.

Security and Privacy is the major challenge for the connected world. We build security and privacy into the core of Pixel devices to help end users and business owners to manage existing and incoming security challenges. We bring the most innovative security technologies and features into Pixel devices and also Android ecosystems. The open source software projects we collaborate on, run on ARM CPUs which constitute the largest share of smartphones market and an increasing number of hyper-scale data center and cloud computing machines.

The Google Pixel team focuses on designing and delivering the world's most helpful mobile experience. The team works on shaping the future of Pixel devices and services through some of the most advanced designs, techniques, products, and experiences in consumer electronics. This includes bringing together the best of Google’s artificial intelligence, software, and hardware to build global smartphones and create transformative experiences for users across the world.

  • Participate in, or lead design reviews with peers and stakeholders to decide amongst available technologies.
  • Review code developed by other developers and provide feedback to ensure best practices (e.g., style guidelines, checking code in, accuracy, testability, and efficiency).
  • Develop technical solutions to help mitigate security vulnerabilities, and contribute to upstream open source software projects.
  • Triage product or system issues and debug/track/resolve by analyzing the sources of issues and the impact on hardware, network, or service operations and quality.

Minimum qualifications:

  • Bachelor’s degree or equivalent practical experience.
  • 5 years of experience with software development in one or more programming languages.
  • 3 years of experience testing, maintaining, or launching software products.
  • 1 year of experience with software design and architecture.

Preferred qualifications:

  • Master's degree or PhD in Computer Science or related technical field.
  • 1 year of experience in a technical leadership role.
  • Experience in embedded or phone security design, including authentication, encryption, certificate management, and operating system security.
  • Experience with boot and runtime firmwares, such as TF-A, UEFI, and ACPI.
  • Familiarity with low-power SoCs and various CPU architectures (e.g., ARM, RISC-V, x86, MIPS).

title: Senior UX Researcher, YouTube Shorts Ads
descriptionHtml:
At Google, we "Focus on the user and all else will follow." As a User Experience Researcher (UXR), you make this possible. You will join our multi-disciplinary UX team, collaborating with Engineering and Product Management, to gather insights and create industry-leading products.

You’ll play a critical role in helping your team understand user needs and will drive impact at all stages of product development, ensuring products are useful, usable, and helpful. You will explore user behaviors and motivations by conducting primary research, including: field studies, interviews, diary studies, ethnography, surveys, usability testing, and logs analysis. You will also grow within a supportive UXR community offering mentorship, regular meetups, and exclusive internal tools.

As a UX Researcher in YouTube Ads UX, you will lead viewer research across YouTube Shorts. You will be instrumental in defining how we optimize the health and pacing of the Shorts ad experience while shaping new interactive, shoppable, and brand and sponsorship ad formats within the shorts feed.

Google Ads is at the forefront of AI innovation, applying cutting-edge machine learning and Generative AI models like Gemini to power a multi-billion dollar global business.

Our work directly impacts billions of users by protecting users from harm, improving ad quality, and optimizing campaigns for advertiser return-on-investment. We foster a culture of deep collaboration, partnering closely with teams like Google Research and DeepMind to solve complex challenges. Join us to work on state-of-the-art AI, take on problems at an unparalleled scale, and build the next generation of advertising technology.

Individual pay is determined by factors including job-related skills, experience, and relevant education or training.

US: $159000 - $230000 (USD) + 15% bonus target + equity + benefits

Learn more about benefits at Google.

Responsibilities

  • Develop a research roadmap addressing product and business questions using methods such as remote in-depth interviews, diary studies, prototype testing, surveys, and logs analysis.

  • Represent viewer needs and expectations to UX, Product Management, and Engineering to ensure product decisions support creator and advertiser goals.

  • Partner with core YouTube Shorts product teams, Go-to-Market leads, and horizontal Ads teams to create a cohesive viewer experience.

Minimum qualifications:

  • Experience in mixed methods research, including qualitative (e.g., in-depth interviews, diary studies) and quantitative (e.g., surveys, log analysis) approaches.
  • Experience producing business impact through applied research.

Preferred qualifications:

  • Master's degree or PhD in Human-Computer Interaction, Cognitive Science, Statistics, Psychology, Anthropology, or related field.
  • 5 years of experience conducting UX research on products and working with executive leadership (e.g., Director level and above).
  • 3 years of experience managing projects, and working in a large, matrixed organization.

title: Data Center Facilities Technician, Electrical
descriptionHtml:
The Data Center team designs and operates some of the most sophisticated electrical engineering, mechanical engineering and HVAC systems in the world. Facilities Technicians at Google data centers operate, monitor and support physical facilities conditions. Some of these duties will include heating and cooling of air and water, power supply, generators, UPS systems, electrical distribution and control and monitoring systems. You regularly help inspect, maintain and repair various data center systems such as piping and non-critical electrical or mechanical system components).

As an advocate for best practices, you develop creative approaches to reducing operational costs while improving overall data center efficiency. You ensure that environmental and safety standards are consistently met, identifying problems and making repairs quickly. In emergency situations or abnormal conditions, you manage data center performance issues and outages to minimize the recovery time from failures.

As a Facilities Technician, you will operate, monitor, and support physical facilities conditions for the data centers.

In this role, you will be required to co-lead and ensure the electrical system compliance including local legal and Environmental Health and Safety (EHS) policies. You will work to ensure electrical system reliability, and co-lead the commissioning activities on functional tests and Integrated System Test (IST). Additionally, you will manage and support electrical system operation, and co-lead the electrical system maintenance program including preparing the technical specification, procurement and maintenance vendor performance management.

The Data Center team designs and operates some of the most sophisticated electrical and HVAC systems in the world. We are a diverse, upbeat, creative, team-oriented group of engineers committed to building and operating powerful data centers.

Responsibilities

  • Responsible for electrical system but not only limited to extra high voltage/medium voltage system's for the uptime, maintenance, operation, troubleshooting, and repair of electrical equipment in a data center environment.
  • Conduct root cause analysis for service failures, implement recovery and prevention actions, and drive continuous improvement in site water usage effectiveness and power usage effectiveness to minimize environmental impact and enhance system reliability.
  • Lead and support startup, commissioning, and integration of new equipment and systems into facilities infrastructure, and coordinate vendor support for repairs and project implementation. 
  • Ensure compliance with all site environmental health, safety policies, and legal requirements, while developing infrastructure knowledge and providing training to the team.
  • Maintain operational availability by working rotating shifts, including weekends and holidays.

Minimum qualifications:

  • Associate's degree, trade school certification, or other certified training in a related technical field, or equivalent practical experience.
  • 7 years of Electrical experience (e.g., electrical testing equipment or electrical distribution) in an industrial or commercial environment.
  • Ability to participate in material handling tasks such as lifting, carrying or moving up to 50 lbs (23 kg) of equipment, the required use of safety equipment such as limited weight bearing work platforms, ladders, step stools and personal protective equipment (PPE) like safety harnesses in accordance with safety and ergonomic guidelines and assessments.
  • Ability to work non-standard hours and work rotations/shifts.

Preferred qualifications:

  • 5 years of experience in the facilities field including operating and maintaining mission critical facilities (data centers, hospitals, pharma, semiconductor, refineries, power plants, etc.).
  • Experience working as an electrical engineer (JEK) or as a professional engineer with practicing certification or registered as an energy manager.
  • Experience with safety rules and regulations associated with operating complex infrastructure.
  • Experience with electrical components, or as a chargeman with Suruhanjaya Tenaga (ST).
  • Ability to perform maintenance on electrical or controls systems and capable of independently resolving common system failures.
